source.title: Trajectory-dependent Generalization Bounds for Deep Neural Networks via Fractional Brownian Motion
source.authors: Cheng-Li Tan; Jiang Zhang; Jun-Min Liu; Yihong Gong

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a complete paper, but its title differs from the supplied title: the text is titled “Learning Non-Vacuous Generalization Bounds from Optimization.”
record.tranche_reason: The study measures generalization gaps and compares them with an optimizer-dependent bound while varying training-set size and the learning-rate-to-mini-batch-size ratio. These are related measures and settings, but it does not test the claim versions’ specific interventions or measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses random-label memorization and several generalization measures only as cited prior work; those are not this study’s results. Figures 5–8 and 10 show study results, but the supplied text does not give recoverable point values. Figures 7–8 vary learning rate and mini-batch size together, so their effects cannot be isolated.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates a trajectory-based generalization-bound estimator, not any of V1–V8. Its nearest comparison to V5 jointly varies learning rate and batch size and reports loss gaps without establishing a fixed epoch budget or a batch-size effect on held-out performance. It does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness for V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they propose a tractable, non-vacuous bound for SGD and report empirical agreement with loss-gap trends across training-set sizes and learning-rate-to-batch-size ratios, plus plausible ImageNet-1K estimates. These are empirical estimates using assumptions and approximations; extending the theoretical results to adaptive optimizers remains future work despite the AdamW ImageNet experiments.
record.recipe_differences: The study estimates an algorithm-dependent generalization bound from stochastic-gradient-noise trajectories; it does not reproduce the interventions or measurements specified in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The estimated bound changes with training-set size and the learning-rate-to-mini-batch-size ratio; the study also reports results for constant versus cosine-annealed learning rates.

fits_no_version.finding: For ResNet-56 and WideResNet-28-10 on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, the estimated bound and measured loss gap decrease with training-set size under constant and cosine learning-rate schedules.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A trajectory-based generalization-bound estimator tracks loss-gap changes across training-set sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.3 and Figures 7–8 report decreasing estimated bounds with increasing learning-rate-to-batch-size ratio and show corresponding generalization gaps. Learning rate and batch size are varied jointly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization bounds and loss gaps vary across joint learning-rate and batch-size sweeps.

fits_no_version.finding: On ImageNet-1K, the reported maximum loss gaps and final estimated bounds are respectively 0.25 and 0.33 for ResNet-18, and 0.5 and 0.6 for ViT-S-32.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The estimated bound approaches the measured loss gap late in ImageNet-1K training.

fits_no_version.finding: Across training-set sizes, the proposed Hausdorff-dimension estimate decreases, persistent-homology dimension increases, and the upper Blumenthal–Getoor index remains near 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different fractal complexity estimators respond differently to increasing training-set size.

record.problems: The bound relies on stated assumptions, including countable data support and a condition on the driving noise. The paper notes that stopping time affects the results. The learning-rate and mini-batch-size sweeps vary both together. Several plotted results have no recoverable point values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the reported results concern a proposed generalization-bound estimator and measured generalization gaps, not the specific outcomes named by V1–V8. Plot-only curves are not reconstructed as numeric rows.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Comparative held-out performance of adaptive optimizers and SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Large- versus small-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets, including whether recipe adaptations remove a penalty.
Effects of adding or removing dropout on held-out error.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance and its ranking of generalization gaps against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Correct V5 from tested_not_extracted to not tested. The record incorrectly describes a negative correlation between the bound and generalization gap: the stated negative correlation is between the bound and learning-rate-to-batch-size ratio. Section 4.4 also specifies basic ImageNet preprocessing/augmentation despite Section 4.1's blanket statement that augmentation is unused. No claim-relevant rows are missing; rows_left_out already declares the related estimator results.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold and resulting test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer held-out performance.
The study varies learning rate and mini-batch size together, so it does not isolate large-batch effects or establish the fixed-epoch comparison in the version.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized training examples and the effect on test accuracy.
